dek: A Las Vegas radio regular who has sold picks for more than two decades: through the Jim Feist network and 1 900 lines in 2002, his own ScottWins.com until about 2018, and Doc's Sports since April 2018. Packages run from $25 a day to $850 a season, losing packages earn more picks or store credit, and every record on his page is a run chosen by the seller. One of those runs, "NFL: 414-367, 58%," works out to 53%.

short_answer: Scott Spreitzer is a real, named handicapper with a long Las Vegas media history, and he has sold picks for at least 24 years. A saved copy of ScottWins.com from November 2002 forwards to his page on the Jim Feist network, selling three play packages for $10 on 1 900 phone lines. By 2012 ScottWins.com was his own storefront, and in April 2018 Doc's Sports announced he would sell exclusively through its site. Doc's names its operator, publishes its prices and has sold picks since 1971. In that narrow sense, buying his picks is a legitimate transaction.

Whether Spreitzer's picks actually make money is a separate matter. His Doc's page shows about 30 runs and totals, all chosen by the seller, and no full log. We checked them by hand. Most percentages match their win and loss counts, but "NFL: 414-367, 58%" is 53.0%, barely above the 52.4% needed at -110. Comparing the same page on 7 Nov and 20 Nov 2026, his running football total fell from +15,360 to +14,820, his NBA total from +21,405 to +20,895, and his props total by about $550, while the page led with a 63% run over the last seven weeks.

Independent buyer talk is close to nil: two short critical forum remarks from 2005 and 2011, one 2014 comment on his radio sales style, and 2026 forum members reposting his plays without results. We found no complaints about billing or refunds, and no praise from buyers. Treat him as a seller with marketing records, not a proven winner. If you buy, buy short, record every pick yourself, and judge it over a few hundred picks.

guarantee: Every Spreitzer package is sold under the Doc's Sports guarantee. On weekly and monthly packages the page says that if the package "finishes at a loss, you can extend your service for free through our self-extend program." Days with no picks "do not qualify for extra days unless the package fails to produce a profit."

On one day packages the remedy is an account credit, usually $30, added the next morning around 11 a.m. Eastern. The page says "Extend mode is no longer available" on daily sales. Some daily packages count a small win as a failure: college basketball pays the credit unless the day makes at least $40, NHL unless it makes at least $35.
Season and full year packages carry no guarantee wording on his page.

Doc's terms and conditions say: "Once a product or service has been purchased and delivered or viewed, there are no refunds." They add that "In most cases Doc's Sports does in fact guarantee its services," usually by extending the account. The terms also say an account found sharing logins "will be canceled with no refund." Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and those are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: we read his Doc's Sports page on 7 Nov and again on 20 Nov 2026, divided wins by wins plus losses for each run, and compared the running totals between the two dates. The percentages and the movement between dates come only from his own page, so this tests whether the page is consistent, not whether the picks were graded honestly.

Two findings stand out. First, the NFL line is labeled 58% but its own numbers give 53.0%. Second, over 13 days in which the page led with "63% L7 WEEKS!", the long running football, NBA and props totals all went down. Both are true at once: a seven week window can be hot while the last two weeks lose. The window the page leads with is the one that looks best.

Dollar figures assume $100 per unit, and his plays are rated from 2 to 7 units, so a dollar total can be large even when the win rate is ordinary. Several runs start on dates the seller picked, such as 1 Oct for the 32-19 run. The 2018 ScottWins.com page said "ALL RECORDS ARE MONITORED," but named no monitor.

The contest claims are the most checkable kind of claim, because casinos run those contests. We searched for the Station Casinos and Westgate SuperContest results he cites and found no outside page confirming them. That does not mean they are false; it means we could not verify them.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. Scott Spreitzer does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming Scott Spreitzer most often were BuzzKill (TheRX newsletters thread), 1218Sports, TheGodOfCappers, EZMSports. From 22 Sep 2026 to 15 Nov 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a Scott Spreitzer block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.

Result: 3 wins and 5 losses on 8 plays, -2.27 units, or -28.4% per unit risked. By sport: the NFL plays split 2 and 2, -0.18 units. By month: September 0 won, 1 lost, -1.00 units; October 3 won, 2 lost, +0.73 units; November 0 won, 2 lost, -2.00 units.
What it means: eight graded Spreitzer plays are far short of a sample that could settle anything.

What a buyer can verify independently: nothing current. A third party contest result would count, and his bio cites two, but we found no casino or news page confirming either. We found no court or regulator record involving him.

What Spreitzer and Doc's publish: runs and totals by sport, chosen by the seller, and a daily note on whether yesterday won (for example "Scott Spreitzer went 0-1 Thursday" in the NHL and "0-1 in MLS Thursday" on 20 Nov 2026). We found no full, time stamped log of every paid pick with the line, the odds and the release time. His free picks are posted one at a time, each listed as "Offered at: BookMaker."

History we could confirm from saved pages: in November 2002 scottwins.com forwarded to his handicapper page on jimfeist.com, which sold "all 3 releases" for $10 on 1 900 and 1 800 numbers and promoted a "perfect 6-0" weekend. In January 2012 ScottWins.com was his own store (phone 1 866 439 6758) with a roster of other handicappers. On 1 Jan 2018 it still sold his plays by email and claimed a "15-2-2, 87% winning run." Doc's announced him on 11 Apr 2018 as its new handicapper, with service from 12 Apr. By April 2022 the scottwins.com domain was listed for sale, and a 2021 copy showed unrelated content.

About the store: Doc's Sports says it has operated since 1971 and is owned by its founder, Morey "Doc" Moseman. Its FAQ sets a goal "to hit at least 60% or better" and says "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in." Its roster showed 14 handicappers on 20 Nov 2026.

our_data.text: In this edition no Scott Spreitzer pick account is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: his page advertises runs from 53% (NFL, by our math) to 63% (last seven weeks), and Doc's own FAQ sets a goal of 60% winners.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Scott Spreitzer is close to nonexistent. We found no buyer describing a purchase, good or bad, on any site. What exists is a handful of forum remarks over 21 years.

customers.text: Across Sportsbook Review, TheRX, Reddit, the BBB, Trustpilot and CapperTek we found six forum items and no buyer reviews. The three critical ones are short opinions with no purchase details: a 2005 TheRX post lumping him with other Vegas sellers, a 2011 Sportsbook Review reply naming him among the worst touts, and a 2014 Sportsbook Review post complaining about his loud radio sales style. In September 2026 TheRX members reposted one of his plays and one wished him luck on a 7 unit college football play, with no result posted. TheRX lists him among services whose write ups may not be posted. Our saved copy of the main betting subreddits had no posts or comments naming him. We found no complaints about billing or refunds, no BBB or Trustpilot reviews, and no buyer praise either. There is simply not enough independent evidence to judge his service from customers.

In a TheRX Friday service play thread, a member reposted "Sprietzer 7 U CFB" and asked if anyone could confirm the side; another member said it was Indiana -20.5 and a third wished him luck. Nobody posted the result or said they had bought from him.

TheRX forum's service play rules list Scott Spreitzer among the services whose write ups members may not post. The rule says nothing about his results or customer experience; it only shows he is treated there as a paid seller.

In a Sportsbook Review thread about another handicapper, a member praised that handicapper's calm style and contrasted it with sellers who scream on the radio, naming Spreitzer. It is a comment on his sales style, not his results.

In a Sportsbook Review thread asking members to list the worst touts they had seen, one member replied with just two names, one of them Spreitzer. They gave no reasons, no purchase details and no record, so this is an unsupported opinion, not evidence.

In a 2005 TheRX thread about another handicapper, a member joked that Las Vegas sellers including Spreitzer and Jim Feist come out of the same school for touts. It is a general jab at the industry with no purchase or result behind it.
A Better Business Bureau search for "Scott Spreitzer" returned no results, and Trustpilot listed no reviews of docsports.com, the store he sells through.
CapperTek, a handicapper review site, keeps a page for ScottWins.com under his name, but it shows no reviews or complaints.

Our saved copy of posts and comments from r/sportsbook, r/sportsbetting, r/sportsbettingadvice and r/SportsBettingPicks contained no mention of Spreitzer, and web searches found no Covers thread about buying his picks. For buyer reports on the store he sells through, see our Doc's Sports review; those cover the roster in general, not Spreitzer.

conflicts: Spreitzer's free pick on his page on 20 Nov 2026 listed the line as "Offered at: BookMaker," an offshore sportsbook, next to a "Free $60 Account Sign Up" offer. The Doc's FAQ says: "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in." We did not see the terms of any deal between Doc's and BookMaker. Pointing buyers to one named sportsbook is still a possible financial interest a buyer should keep in mind.
Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Before using the BookMaker link on his page, confirm what the law allows where you live.
Every record on his page is published by the store that sells his picks. Doc's does not name an outside monitor.
strengths: A named person with a long, checkable public history: archived pages show him selling picks under his own name since at least 2002.
Sold through a store with a named operator, a mailing address, a phone line, office hours and written terms.
Prices and guarantee terms are written out for every package on his page, from $25 a day.
His page reports losing days in its daily notes (for example 0-1 in the NHL and MLS on 19 Nov 2026), not only wins.
Free picks and a free account offer on Doc's let a reader see his style before buying.
concerns: No full public record. Every number on his page is a run or total chosen by the seller, often from a start date the seller picked.
At least one headline figure is wrong by its own numbers: "NFL: 414-367, 58%" is 53.0%.
In the 13 days we compared, his long running football, NBA and props totals all fell while the page led with a 63% seven week run.
The guarantee replaces a losing package with more picks or store credit, season packages have none, and Doc's terms say there are no refunds once picks are delivered or viewed.
Contest wins cited in his bio could not be confirmed in any outside source we opened.
His free picks name an offshore sportsbook, and the store's FAQ recommends offshore books.
checklist: Request twelve months of Spreitzer releases with line, odds, unit size and send time for each. His page's hand picked runs are not a record.
Do the math on any record: divide wins by wins plus losses. His NFL line labeled 58% is 53%.
Note the running totals on his page the day you buy and check them again when your package ends. They show whether the period you paid for won.
Count units, not wins. With plays from 2 to 7 units, a few big losers can sink a good win rate.
Scan each guarantee for refund, credit or extension wording. Here every version is more picks or credit, and season packages have no guarantee.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get at a licensed sportsbook.
faq: He is a real handicapper with a long Las Vegas radio history who has sold picks under his own name since at least 2002, and he now sells through Doc's Sports, which names its operator and publishes its prices. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because no full record of every pick is published, and one of his headline figures does not match its own numbers.
What does the Watchdog sample of Scott Spreitzer show?
We graded 8 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 22 Sep 2026 to 15 Nov 2026: 3 won, 5 lost, -2.27 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.
How much does Scott Spreitzer cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 his Doc's Sports page sold one day packages for $25 to $30, weekly packages for $89 to $99, monthly packages for $279 to $325, and season packages from $495 (rest of football season) to $850 (NBA). The 365 day soccer package was $795.

No cash refunds. Doc's Sports rules out refunds after a package has been delivered or viewed. Losing weekly and monthly packages can be extended for free, losing day packages earn a $30 account credit, and season packages carry no guarantee.
Does Scott Spreitzer have a verified record?

No current one that we could find. His page shows runs such as 32-19 since 1 Oct and 525-419 on top plays, chosen and graded by the store that sells him. The contest results in his bio were not confirmed by any outside page we opened.
Where did Scott Spreitzer sell picks before Doc's Sports?

Saved web pages show scottwins.com forwarding to his page on the Jim Feist network in 2002, with $10 plays sold on 1 900 lines, then ScottWins.com as his own store from at least 2011 to early 2018. Doc's announced him in April 2018, and by 2022 the ScottWins.com domain was listed for sale.

For the money you get his picks in several sports with unit ratings, from a known name, with $25 to $30 daily entry points. What is unproven is whether those picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays; his own NFL line works out to 53%, and a losing package only earns more of the same picks.
